tool: SAML-tracer, HAR files and the decoders, with Keycloak's logs
why_this_tool: A runbook is learned by producing each failure on purpose where you can see both sides, and the local Keycloak and node-saml setup from the earlier paths lets you break the audience, the ACS, the clock, the secret, the code and the scope one at a time while capturing with the tools a customer call allows (a tracer, a HAR, a log). The error rows that came from the learning center's runs are verbatim; the vendor rows are from the official references.
alternatives: Burp Suite with the SAML Raider extension edits and replays SAML messages for deeper testing; jwt_tool and the step CLI decode and test tokens from the shell; a customer's sandbox tenant with its sign-in logs is the best place to see the vendor side; the Entra test-SSO page and Okta's system log need an account the learning center did not create.

setup.do: Have the SAML practice path's Keycloak IdP and node-saml SP running, and the OpenID Connect path's public client configured; install the SAML-tracer extension in Firefox or Chrome.
setup.done_when: A SAML login and an OIDC login both succeed in the browser and the tracer icon shows messages when you log in.
setup.why: The runbook is practised by breaking a working setup; both flows have to work first.

setup.do: Keep three things open: the browser's Network tab (with 'preserve log' on), the SAML lesson's two-line decoder (or samltool.com for local messages only), and the JWT decode one-liner from the token lesson.
setup.done_when: You can decode a SAMLRequest, a SAMLResponse and a JWT from a capture in under a minute each.

source.title: OneLogin SAML tools: decode SAML messages

setup.why: Capture and decode are the first two steps of every call; having the tools ready is the preparation.

steps.do: With the tracer recording, run the SAML login; export the trace; identify the AuthnRequest and the Response and read, from the trace, the Destination, the AssertionConsumerServiceURL, the Issuer, the Audience, the NameID and the signature elements.
steps.done_when: Your export is saved and you can point at each of the six values in it.
steps.why: The tracer is the first tool on any SSO ticket; reading a good trace once makes the bad ones legible.

steps.do: With the Network tab recording, run the OIDC login and save the HAR; run the HAR-reading script from the lesson and find the redirect that carries the code and state, and the token request that follows.
steps.done_when: The script prints the redirect chain with the callback Location containing code and state, and you can say which entries would be sensitive in a customer's HAR.
steps.why: A HAR is what a customer can send you without any extension; knowing where the flow is in it is the skill.

steps.do: Paste the local SAMLResponse (never a customer's) into the samltool.com decoder, and inflate the SAMLRequest from the redirect with the Python two-liner; compare the two results with the tracer's.
steps.done_when: All three decodings agree, and you know which tool you would use with no extension and no script available.

source.title: OneLogin SAML tools: decode SAML messages

steps.why: The decoders are interchangeable; the rule about customer data is not.

steps.do: Break the SP's audience (set it to a different string), log in, and read the exact error from the SP; restore it.
steps.done_when: The SP rejects with an audience error text you have recorded verbatim, and the tracer shows the Audience in the assertion unchanged.

source.title: Microsoft Entra: Debug SAML-based single sign-on to applications

steps.why: Audience mismatch is the most common SAML failure after certificates; the error text is a runbook row.

steps.do: Break the ACS: change the SP's callback URL to a path Keycloak does not have registered, log in, and read the error on the IdP's page and in its log; restore it.
steps.done_when: Keycloak refuses the AuthnRequest with an invalid-request error naming the ACS or redirect, and the row is recorded.
steps.why: ACS and redirect URI mismatches fail on the IdP side before the SP sees anything; knowing which side errs is half the diagnosis.

steps.do: Set the SP's accepted clock skew to 0 and shift the SP's idea of time by a few minutes (or wait for an assertion to age past NotOnOrAfter), log in, and read the error; restore the skew.
steps.done_when: The SP rejects with a 'not yet valid' or 'expired' style error, and you can state what skew a production SP should accept.

source.title: Microsoft Entra: Debug SAML-based single sign-on to applications

steps.why: Clock errors look random to users ('works on one node'); seeing the exact text once makes them recognisable.

steps.do: Produce the OIDC failures on purpose: a token request with a wrong client secret, a replayed authorization code, a request with an unregistered redirect_uri, and a userinfo call with a token lacking the openid scope. Record error and error_description from each response body.
steps.done_when: Four rows: 401 unauthorized_client or invalid_client, 400 invalid_grant, the IdP's redirect_uri error page, and 403 from userinfo; all with the verbatim text.
steps.why: The RFC's error codes have exact meanings; a table of them with real text stops the guessing on a call.

steps.do: Raise Keycloak's log level for the SAML and OIDC protocol categories and the events category, repeat two of the failures, and find each in the container log.
steps.done_when: The log shows a line for each rejection with the reason, and you can say which category produced it.
steps.why: The IdP's log is the vendor-side evidence; a local IdP is the only one whose log you can read in full.

steps.do: Read the Entra SAML debugging page and the error codes reference, and (needs a free account; not run by the learning center) run 'Test single sign-on' on an enterprise application to download the SAML request and read the resolution guidance; read Okta's error codes reference and find E0000004 and E0000011.
steps.done_when: You can describe what the Entra test button does and name three AADSTS codes and two Okta codes with their causes.

source.title: Microsoft Entra: authentication and authorization error codes

steps.why: Customers paste these codes into tickets; recognising them saves the first round trip.

steps.do: Build the runbook table with at least ten rows from the steps above and the lesson's lists: symptom, exact error text, cause, fix, which capture showed it. Add the three SFTP and webhook rows from the machine-to-machine and file feed lessons.
steps.done_when: The table has ten or more rows with verbatim error text in each, and a colleague could use it on a call without you.
steps.why: The table is the runbook; every incident after this adds a row.
